newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-DEPLETED NANTES LOOK TO THE NEW WAVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEPLETED NANTES LOOK TO THE NEW WAVE.

text.p: Any child playing on the beach will have experienced some of the frustrations associated with running Nantes.
"This club is like a sandcastle you have to rebuild after each tide. But it doesn't work so bad," said goalkeeper Mickael Landreau.
The longest serving club in the French first division and champions in 1995, Nantes appear to start every new season with the slate washed clean.
The tide has been especially high this year, sweeping away the last two big-name players of the 1995 season, Chad's Japhet N'doram, who left for Monaco, and Claude Makelele, who joined Marseille.
After losing Christian Karembeu and Patrice Loko two years ago, Nicolas Ouedec and Reynald Pedros last year, coach Jean-Claude Suaudeau has decided to quit.
He will be replaced by Reynald Denoueix who was in charge of the youth training centre.
Denoueix will also have to do without two other key players, Christophe Pignol and Eddy Capron, transferred to Monaco and Rennes respectively, when the French season starts on Friday.

Nantes' annual problems have strictly financial reasons. The team lost 15 millions francs last season ($2.5 million) and the debt is expected to reach 52 million francs ($9 million) at the end of next season.
The municipality, which has a share in the club's administration, asked for tough measures to be taken in order to stop the trend.
For the same reason, recruits have been few -- defender Stephane Lievre joined from Caen and striker Samba N'Diaye from St Etienne.
As usual, Nantes had to rely on their youth once more and five players from the club's youth centre have signed their first professional contract.
Landreau has now become something of a fixture but he became first choice goalkeeper at 17 in the season after Nantes won their last title.
"It's become a habit but it is too much. We've gone through this too often," said Suaudeau before quitting as coach last week.
"It is all the harder as we always aim at staying among France's top five or six teams."
After N'Doram's departure Jocelyn Gourvennec became Nantes new skipper and he said he believed the miracle would work out again.
"There is harmony in this team which started when we were struggling last year and we're trying to keep the spirit," said the 25-year-old playmaker.
"Actually, the French first division has not changed much. There are a couple of big teams and behind them it's pretty open. I think our chances of doing well this season are intact."
Last year Nantes made a pathetic start, slumping to 18th place before a streak of 31 victories lifted them to third.
